Bobroff fall from grace

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Personal injury attorney Ronald Bobroff have built their lucractive practice on ripping off clients with a contingency fee agreement - now the foundations of their schemes are beginning to crumble

Summary:
RBP has recently been on the receiving end of numerous adverse judgments in several courts, including the Supreme Court of Appeal (SCA) and the Ronald Bobroff head of SA largest personal injury and medical negligence practice, in public portrays himself as an ethical legal professional with the interests of the public and his clients at heart. But in private it seems that Bobroff and his son Darren have over the years milked the Road Accident Fund and his clients of millions, that he may now have to pay back.


Further information:
A series of rulings found that RBP’s common law contingency fee agreements are unlawful and that the firm grossly overcharged several vehicle accident victims it represented at the Road Accident Fund (RAF). Several judgments also suggest that Ronald and Darren Bobroff may be guilty of improper conduct. This could result in their names being struck from the roll of attorneys.
But if it’s the end of the line for Bobroff, he is going down fighting.
Right now Bobroff is waging a battle on many fronts. Whistleblowers with intimate knowledge of his company have come forward, patients backed by court rulings can show how they have been ripped off and Tony Beamish Moneyweb investigative journalist, has exposed the company’s rotten dealings in a series of public articles.

Despite this, RBP continues to try and justify its contingency fee agreements on the basis of a determination by The Law Society of the Northern Provinces (LSNP).

Here are short summaries of the most notable judgments against the company.
• In the case of Juanne De La Guerre, the Constitutional Court ruled that RBP’s common law contingency fee arrangement is illegal. The facts of the case show that RBP charged her R 1 073 000. The court has already ordered RBP to pay back R508 000.
• In the case of Anthony de Pontes, the South Gauteng High Court (SGHC) ordered RBP to refund de Pontes R2.1million. RBP charged him R 2 101 871, but has only been able to justify at most R400 905. RBP has already paid back R800 000. A request for leave to appeal was denied. Bobroff viewing

02/03/2015 01:28:58 PM

George/Amalia/Wynand
1. You start by defaming him. You haven’t set up the situation yet. You must only go to the over-reaching later. It’s strong but it needs to come once we have seen that it happened
2. Journalism doesn’t feel objective.
3. Anthony Millar comes across as biased, very angry, not objective.
4. Don’t start the story by making it about Cora/Tony/Anthony...
5. Rather start with the case studies... start with Da Ponte, tell the human story, - here is a lawyer who took the money.
6. Millar doesn’t come across as objective, he seems very emotional and angry.
7. Take Tony out of the story completely. Also don’t represent him as a moneyweb journalist.
8. The Paul O Sullivan elements – we need to give him right of reply.
9. Check the old story you have taken visuals from to see if in 2009 he told us anything about his fees and the way he charges.
10. Take out shot of Bobroff in a speedo
11. People won’t understand the Erin Brokowitch principal... please explain it...
12. We don’t see enough of what happened to Yasmin...
13. Explain that Yasmin is a teacher/why we are seeing her in a classroom...
14. Do you have it in a document that prove that he wouldn’t sign the Da Ponte documents unless Da ponte signed the documents himself? Can we therefore add this in?
15. Blur Bobroff wife in the photo
16. Darren and his wife – very confusing who they are... say his daughter in law his son darren’s wife. Script differently.
17. You need to clarify him paying back the fees to some of the clients.
18. Can you put in more line items like R50 000 for photo copies?
19. The numbers don’t tally – on one of the cases he took 910 000 you say, then mention 850 000 and later you say this case study got R3mn?

ERIC – legal
1. Thinks bobroff will sue. Sources are only millar, tony, cora... documents and judgement. Joy: there are documents to back up everything we say. Tony: we know he won’t sue for defamation as he hasn’t done so with all the stuff written about him. Joy: we have concourt judgment, joy hasn’t looked at 2013 judgment but Tony has. The judgment for the law society – Marcus and Trengrove gave an opinion in 2004 and 2005 and then a junior gave an opion Etienne Labuschagne that you can but don’t get caught. Joy : also have law society opinion on the hours and charges and the overreaching – but its only in front of the investigating committee – its not a disciplinary.
2. Stay within a fair and accurate report of what has happened within court proceedings
3. Turn it around and focus on the case studies. Eric – do we have the ltter that summonses him to the investigating committee? JOY: no only their report where they say come and explain the 10 things we list as charges.

EXCLUDED FROM STORY: After the court found against Bobroff he wrote a letter to the law society colleagues – Joy hasn’t included the comments from it in this cut

BOBROFF INTERVIEW: Ronald says this is a vendetta by discovery and everyone is doing their bidding. If we get an interview with Bobroff, he will mention Discovery. We have Jonathan Broomberg at 5 tomorrow afternoon in case Ronald gives us an interview...


Bobroff viewing 2
Wednesday 11 March 2015
9.30am

GM, Eric, Joy, Tony, AC, WG

1. Duration should be 18 minutes

2. Bobroff chasing ambulance image should be removed. Rather use older footage of him.
3. Newsletter explanation is a bit confusing. Dumb this down. Bring out the points in bold in graphics where it actually states that on the newsletter.
4. R6 a copy is that industry standard? Check this.
5. Contingency agreement – see where it says 30% on document. Explain that act allows for 25% or double whichever is lower.
6. Take out Devi comment... “Let’s move on” in Bobroff interview.
7. Write around the issue that Bobroff charged for additional 16 hours after the case was settled on De Pontes. Add response from Bobroff here.
8. Law Society Certificate: bring it out and show the viewer what it says. Pull out words: partners never found guilty...
9. Take out other two people on Darren Bobroff picture
10. Where you say Anthony was unaware that he was signing 30% contract, explain the legal issues here about percentage.
11. Rather say “Bobroff ignored subsequent 2004 supreme court of appeal judgement which held...”. Use appeal court visuals here.
12. Quote Fabricius comment on de la Guerre matter. Include his name.
13. Take out double reference to “Plus Vat” on letter
14. Cover Anthony Millar’s numberplate
15. Add Devi asking Bobroff about charging for 16 hours after settlement was reached
16. 2 epilepsy comments on De La Guerre
17. Check on de la Guerre figure. R1.1-million or R969 000? Double check this.
18. Rather use law “reinterpreted” instead of re-engineered.
19. Don’t use image of Tony with De la Guerres
20. RAF victims could go back for recourse with interest going back all the 2002. Make this clearer. “Any claimant of the fund can go back....”
21. Discovery saying: no two sides. Take out.
22. RAF exterior shot rather than interior first
23. Leave out Paul O’ Sullivan
24. Let Cora explain more about being a Russian spy. Clarify her qualifications and she was in SA Navy.
25. confusing where you bring Jeanne in where you refer to Cora again as being moved into the accounts dept at the same time Jeanne’s case went to the Con Court.

Legal: Eric van den Bergh
1. “If he is honest...” Can’t have like that. Take that commentary out.
2. Legally it is sound.
3. All comments are backed up.
4. Add: Even the constitutional court observed there was confusion in the legal profession about contingency fees.
5. Add he says everyone is doing it. He gave contingency agreements from others but none are signed. Put in a line that others are doing it too. We need to say he accuses others.
6. Take out Paul O’ Sullivan entirely and just say Bobroff accused her of theft.
7. Ask Bobroff for recording of Russian spy allegation.
8. Explain Cora was at an American University in Russia and that she was in SA Navy
9. Eric comfortable with link that says overreaching comes down to just plain stealing.

FINAL TX SCRIPT BOBROFF 18th March 2015

Commentary One
Spring 2007- On the P91 near Modderfontein. A driver, racing another smashes into the back of a Hu/nday Accent- two young men are in the back seat, one is killed instantly. The other, Anthony De Pontes barely survives.

UP sound screech brakes

Anthony
I had broken my neck they wanted to amputate my arm and my chances of living weren’t too good

Commentary Two
This apprentice mechanic was paralysed on impact, leaving him confined to his parent’s home for the last eight years.

Anthony
You have to rely on people
It’s everything hey. Dressing me, bathing me feeding me

Commentary Three
Anthony’s family came here to Ronald Bobroff and Partners to help them claim money from the Road Accident Fund.

Link
They trusted he would represent his son’s best interests

Devi to RB
So would you say you run a respectable and ethical business?
Ronald Bobroff
I believe so! I have been elected to the council of the law society and served as a president and held numerous offices within the profession

Commentary Four
But Ronald Bobroff’s image has been tarnished. For years he has been taking a flat percentage off the top of clients money recovered from the RAF. He has charged them common law contingency fees, but these fees are illegal. The De Pontes family didn’t know that. Attorney Anthony Millar explains



Anthony Millar
There is a 1000 years of law that says that type of agreement is prohibited and the reason for that is very simple- that when lawyers become shareholders in their clients cases the professional responsibility to their client and the courts becomes blurred because they now have a vested interest in the outcome of the case.

Commentary Five
In 2010 the RAF paid Anthony R6.1 million. Bobroff took R2.1 Million in fees, including vat. A court later found that Bobroff took R1.7 million more than he should have. Anthony also had to wait for the funds.

Anthony De Pontes
We nearly lost our house – because my parents had to pay for everything.
It really put us in turmoil.

Commentary Six
But Bobroff rejects any allegations of impropriety and he has a Law Society certificate from 2013 as proof.

Ronald Bobroff
We have never had a finding against us of unprofessional conduct. EVER!

Devi Link
The legal profession has a delicate way of describing the theft of a client’s money, by one of their own – they call it over reaching, but when it comes down to it – its just plain stealing

Commentary Seven
Bobroff has been accused of over reaching by two whistleblowers who worked for him, attorney Anthony Millar, Legal journalist Tony Beamish and in January, an investigating committee of the law society.

Devi
The Law Society talks about prima facie evidence of over reaching which is what you say you don’t do?

Ronald
Unfortunately the Chair Mr Mayet seems to lack any understanding of the ruling by the law society on whose committee he actually sits!


Commentary Eight
The Contingency fee act said that attorneys could charge a maximum of 25% or double their normal fees whichever was the lower. Then in 2002 the law society allowed its attorneys to charge more, as long as they were reasonable. Bobroff says he was not alone in charging more.

Bobroff
As you know the law society issued a ruling in 2002 – /where it said its members are permitted and encouraged to charge straight contingency fees
Devi
But that is against the law
Bobroff
Well it wasn’t then

Commentary nine
But as far back as 2004, long before Antony even contacted Bobroff, a high court made a ruling. “Any contingency fee agreement, outside of the act is illegal.”

Devi
It sounds to me like the law said one thing, it was quite clear and lawyers like yourself and others took the gap?
Ronald
I disagree with that, there was not from then till late 2011 a single court decision saying that you could not have a valid common law contingency fee agreement

Commentary Ten
The De Pontes family eventually approached Anthony Millar.

Anthony Millar
Bobroff has taken everything from these clients except responsibility

Commentary eleven
He uncovered additional charges by Bobroff’s firm, which tricked Anthony into making a difficult and unnecessary journey to court, just so they could charge him for the time.

Anthony Millar
There were 16.5 hours of charges for days after the settlement had taken place





Commentary twelve
This is currently one of the counts Bobroff and Partners must answer to, at a discipline/ary enquiry of the Law Society.

Devi to De Pontes
Even if you are a really bad person it would be very difficult to do this to somebody?
Anthony De Pontes
Ya, only a monster would do something like this

Commentary Thirteen
Confirmation that Bobroff and partners were charging unlawfully high fees, would come unexpectedly via this beautiful young woman, flung through the back of a windscreen here, in 2005.

Juanne
I tried to open my eyes but I couldn’t see anything. Nothing! and then I heard my sister scream from far away: “Jeanne is dead, Jeanne is dead!”

Commentary fourteen
Jeannay De la Guerre survived but she’s a broken woman. A brain injury has left her with blackouts, sleeplessness, and on permanent anti-epileptic medication.

Juanne
You just feel like, you know the life is sucked out of you

Commentary fifteen
Juanne also signed Bobroff’s unlawful agreement. Of her R2.5 million payout from the RAF, Bobroff took over a million rand, gave her no bill to explain his costs and made her wait two years for part of her payout.

Did you ever get that bill?
Juanne
No.

Commentary Sixteen
Juanne went to Anthony Millar and together they decided to challenge Bobroff’s agreement in court.

Devi
Where you not scared to take him on he is such a big lawyer?
No.
Why?
Juanne
Because I believe in the law

Commentary Seventeen
But the law was being reinterpreted here, at Bobroff’s office.
Director Darren Bobroff’s letter appears to reverse engineer fees charged to Jeanne, nearly two years after the RAF had paid her out.

PLEASE URGENTLY PREPARE AN ATTORNEY CLIENT BILL SO AS TO ENSURE THAT YOU CAN JUSTIFY THE HOURS FOR A TOTAL FEE PLUS VAT OF R1.1 MILLION

Commentary eighteen
But Ronald blames the secretary.

Ronald
She off her own bat used a standard letter
Devi
You have this as a standard letter?
Ronald
No, no, no- and she took that letter and she changed the wording and she will give evidence under oath that she was not instructed to use that terminology.
It looks bad Ronald! This is what I am saying
Ronald
It does look bad and she has been reprimanded and apologized
Why did you keep her?
Because she is an excellent secretary
Devi
She is not very good
Ronald
Well she is good in other ways

Commentary nineteen
When Anthony requested Jeanne’s bill they were stunned to find a referral fee of R385 thousand paid to Darren Bobroffs wife Lisa, whom she had never met. Ronald blames the bookkeeper.

Ronald
We had a number of bookkeepers who were sadly not up to scratch. What this book keeper did she omitted to debit the fee but next to the cheque she put REF – Referral – there was no referral.

Devi
You are blaming staff again now
Ronald
It was the bookkeeper YES IT WAS!
Devi
Do you have competent people working here now?
Ronald
Very competent
Devi
Why did it go to Darren’s wife though?
Ronald
It was drawings for Darren Bobroff as a director and it was supposed to be deposited in his wife’s account, they were going to buy a property. Perfectly legitimate!

Commentary twenty
In Feb 2013 Juanne De La Guerre won her case against Bobroff.

Judge Fabricius said that Bobroff …”must have been aware that the overwhelming view of distinguished authorities …was that any agreement not complying with the Act would be invalid, and could amount to unprofessional conduct.”

Bobroff appealed and lost.

DEVI link
But despite those judgements Ronald Bobroff pushed on hoping that the Constitutional Court would make a different ruling, but alas for Mr Bobroff they were unequivocal.

Commentary Twenty one
The court confirmed that flat % fees charged by Bobroff and others, had always been illegal. But they also acknowleged confusion around fees.

Bobroff reads judgement
Uncertainty reigned in the attorneys profession!

Devi
Irrespective you were wrong The CC has said so
Ronald
Twelve years after the decision was taken
Devi
Which decision your decision?
Ronald
The Law Society
Devi
The Law Society cannot supercede the law?
Ronald
It can’t.
Devi
Thank you!

Commentary twenty-two
The ruling means that any RAF victims charged these contingency fees outside the act can go back to their lawyers and reclaim the difference with interest.

Devi
You weren’t happy.
Ronald
No
Devi
In fact you called it disastrous
Yes
Devi
For who?
Ronald
For attorneys who acted in good faith in accordance with Law Society guidelines

Commentary twenty- three
The law Society declined an interview with Carte Blanche. They supported Bobroff in his case against Juanne De La Guerre.

Devi
Did the Law society protect Ronald Bobroff
Anthony Millar
I believe so yes …
Devi
How do you feel about that you belong to that same society?
Anthony Millar
I am embarrassed! I am embarrassed at the position!

Commentary twenty- four
Last year legal journalist Tony Beamish pounded out over thirty articles on Bobroff for Moneyweb. Tony now works at Carte Blanche and Bobroff believes we have employed a stooge of Discovery Health.

Ronald
He is singling me out because Discovery has this vendetta against me and me alone.

Commentary Twenty- five
For anything other than illness he says Discovery Health will try to wriggle out of paying your claim.

Ronald
If you require any med care, your neighbors dog bites you, the police assault you, you fall in a hole you are not entitled to any benefits whatsoever and Discovery do enforce that. Its immoral, its illegal, its wrong and by me exposing them Discovery have declared war on me

Commentary Twenty-six
But CEO Jonathan Broomberg says Bobroff’s story is dishonest.
To prove his point he says Discovery Health has paid out 30 000 road accident victims since 2006.

Jonathan
Out of 30 000 we have paid …out find me one who has anything to say apart from this one man and one practice, of the 1100 RAF attorneys find me one who is complaining …you will not find one

Devi
So what is the deal here?

Jonathan
What I think is happening is he is throwing dust in the air, accusing every tom dick and harry of having a vendetta against him – you ask yourself why he is doing that – I would say its to distract attention from his behavior and his practice behavior.


Commentary Twenty-seven
But that is not how Cora Van Der Merwe saw it. A loyal cost consultant employed at Bobroff and partners, Cora felt a duty to protect her boss against Discovery Health and Tony Beamish.

Cora
At one stage he said there is this big vendetta and he will even start crying to get sympathy and your whole heart will go out to him

Commentary Twenty-eight
Later Cora was moved into the legal cost department, and suddenly had access to the legers and the control files. Things just didn’t add up.

Cora
Then I realized that there were a lot of things that concerned me and I got frightened you know.

Devi Link
Apart from the over reaching Cora claims she found evidence of vat fraud, and falsified documents

Commentary Twenty-nine
She also alleges the fees from RAF payments run into millions.

Cora
Well I have evidence that their fees alone in the past 12 months were R49 million. …She smiles… they are 42 years in business

Commentary Thirty
Last year the RAF paid R4.7 billion just in legal fees, but how much have they paid to Ronald Bobroff and partners? Eugene Watson, CEO signed an affidavit in 2013, listing the money they paid to Bobroff and partners over ten years.

Eugene Watson CEO RAF
I think in terms of our figures we showed that almost a billion rand was paid in compensation for over 3000 claims and more than 25% was deemed to be a contingency claim.

Ronald
If it was a billion rand, and I don’t know if it was it represents the damages to our clients, the cost payable to our experts, to our advocates and the amount of our fees. It would certainly not be 25% of a billion rand!!

Devi
Would it be more?
Ronald
No nonsense! Nowhere near that!!

Commentary Thirty- one
Anthony Millar has eight cases against Bobroff. He has broken ranks with the Law Society to tackle Bobroff head on, believing this may be the biggest legal fraud in SA history.

Anthony
I believe we are looking at a R270 million rand fraud at this stage just with what we know

Commentary Thirty- two
By mid 2014 Cora decided to blow the whistle on Bobroff. She felt the Law Society was compromised, and instead made a protected disclosure to journalist Tony Beamish, who she now trusted.

Devi
You accused her of theft
Ronald
She did steal yes. She downloaded electronic information and its probably industrial espionage, but criminal charges will be laid

Commentary Thirty-three
He goes further. Cora could be a Russian agent says Bobroff.

Ronald
I have recordings where she comes to me and says Mr B I want to open my heart to you I have been communicating with Mr Beamish I was trained in counter espionage in the SA navy and I was sent to Russia to train
Devi
She said that to you
Ronald
I have a recording I will make it available to you and she says I have been corresponding with him and I have gained his confidence
Devi
She is a secret agent?
Ronald
That is what she says

Commentary thirty- four
Bobroff never did give Carte Blanche those recordings. While Cora denies being an agent, she admits to studying in Russia in the early 90’s.

Devi
Have you ever been a Russian spy?
No
Have you been to Russia?
Yes

Commentary Thirty- five
By end of Feb last year three levels of the SA judiciary had found Bobroff’s practice illegal, yet Yasmin Motara was still billed using the illegal agreement.

Devi
So what did Ronald Do? Did Ronald stop doing this?
Ronald
Indeed we did.

Commentary Thirty six
When a driver skipped a red light on Snake road, he smashed into Yasmin - her car struck a pole and split in half. Extensive brain injuries forced her to give up her career in politics. Now she just makes it through the day as a teacher.

YASMIN
I have to figure out who is this new me- what cant she do today- what can she get right today, and I try to hide it, because I don’t want people to pity me- but don’t think for a moment that it is not all kinds of hard.

Commentary thirty seven
Yasmin received R6.5 million rand from the RAF, minus Bobroff’s fees of R1.8 million

Yasmin
Well they said don’t worry its R1.8 but we will furnish you with the bill- I haven’t received anything yet – I never heard from Bobroff. Pffff!

Commentary Thirty eight
But Cora had worked on her bill and knew that Yasmin should have paid no more than R362 000, not the R1.8 million that Bobroff had charged her. In December, Cora took Yasmin through the actual charges.

YASMIN
It was so blatant! It was so much! Like photocopies –over R50 000! Really, I would have photocopied it myself.

Commentary thirty nine
Yasmin is currently in a battle with Bobroff to recover some of the funds.

Yasmin
And no one is going to make a buck off my injury! …while RBP get rich!!

Devi
But Anthony it’s the same story over and again?
Anthony
Yes Devi its groundhog day! It’s the same case over and over with the same attorney crying conspiracy and vendetta and all sorts of things, none of it dealing with the bottom line fact that these RAF victims have been grossly over charged on a basis that is illegal

Devi
Don’t you feel bad Ronald
Not at all I feel proud of what we have done
That you took money from people and you were wrong about it and we know you were wrong
Ronald
They got a very good legal service at no cost to themselves in accordance with what the law was understood to be at the time
Devi
And this would have continued if it was not for the De la Guerre matter
Ronald
Everyone would have continued
Devi
And that is not right!
Ronald
I disagree I think it was a great service to the public and I am confident govt will amend the CFA act to make provision for a straight %.


Commentary forty
In the meantime Bobroff is digging deep into his pockets. He has just repaid
Anthony De Pontes R3 million including R700 000 in interest by order of a court, and at least another half a million rand to Jeanne De La Guerre.
But what of his other cases going back to 2002?

Devi
And are you not going to go back and find those cases
Ronald
Definitely not
Devi
And you don’t feel you should from a moral point of view
Ronald
I can’t begin to understand why you would say that?
Devi
I can’t begin to understand why you insist that you wont!
Ronald
Well that is where we differ

THE END

But in private it seems that Bobroff and his son Darren have over the years milked the Road Accident Fund and his clients of millions, that he may now have to pay back. Further information: A series of rulings found that RBP’s common law contingency fee agreements are unlawful and that the firm grossly overcharged several vehicle accident victims it represented at the Road Accident Fund (RAF). Several judgments also suggest that Ronald and Darren Bobroff may be guilty of improper conduct. This could result in their names being struck from the roll of attorneys. But if it’s the end of the line for Bobroff, he is going down fighting. Right now Bobroff is waging a battle on many fronts. Whistleblowers with intimate knowledge of his company have come forward, patients backed by court rulings can show how they have been ripped off and Tony Beamish Moneyweb investigative journalist, has exposed the company’s rotten dealings in a series of public articles. Despite this, RBP continues to try and justify its contingency fee agreements on the basis of a determination by The Law Society of the Northern Provinces (LSNP). Here are short summaries of the most notable judgments against the company. • In the case of Juanne De La Guerre, the Constitutional Court ruled that RBP’s common law contingency fee arrangement is illegal. The facts of the case show that RBP charged her R 1 073 000. The court has already ordered RBP to pay back R508 000. • In the case of Anthony de Pontes, the South Gauteng High Court (SGHC) ordered RBP to refund de Pontes R2.1million. RBP charged him R 2 101 871, but has only been able to justify at most R400 905. RBP has already paid back R800 000. A request for leave to appeal was denied. You start by defaming him. You haven’t set up the situation yet. You must only go to the over-reaching later. It’s strong but it needs to come once we have seen that it happened 2. Journalism doesn’t feel objective. 3. Anthony Millar comes across as biased, very angry, not objective. 4. Don’t start the story by making it about Cora/Tony/Anthony... 5. Rather start with the case studies... start with Da Ponte, tell the human story, - here is a lawyer who took the money. 6. Millar doesn’t come across as objective, he seems very emotional and angry. 7. Take Tony out of the story completely. Also don’t represent him as a moneyweb journalist. 8. The Paul O Sullivan elements – we need to give him right of reply. 9. Check the old story you have taken visuals from to see if in 2009 he told us anything about his fees and the way he charges. 10. Take out shot of Bobroff in a speedo 11. People won’t understand the Erin Brokowitch principal... please explain it... 12. We don’t see enough of what happened to Yasmin... 13. Explain that Yasmin is a teacher/why we are seeing her in a classroom... 14. Do you have it in a document that prove that he wouldn’t sign the Da Ponte documents unless Da ponte signed the documents himself? Can we therefore add this in? 15. Blur Bobroff wife in the photo 16. Darren and his wife – very confusing who they are... say his daughter in law his son darren’s wife. Script differently. 17. You need to clarify him paying back the fees to some of the clients. 18. Can you put in more line items like R50 000 for photo copies? 19. The numbers don’t tally – on one of the cases he took 910 000 you say, then mention 850 000 and later you say this case study got R3mn? ERIC – legal 1. Thinks bobroff will sue. Sources are only millar, tony, cora... documents and judgement. Joy: there are documents to back up everything we say. Tony: we know he won’t sue for defamation as he hasn’t done so with all the stuff written about him. Joy: we have concourt judgment, joy hasn’t looked at 2013 judgment but Tony has. The judgment for the law society – Marcus and Trengrove gave an opinion in 2004 and 2005 and then a junior gave an opion Etienne Labuschagne that you can but don’t get caught. Joy : also have law society opinion on the hours and charges and the overreaching – but its only in front of the investigating committee – its not a disciplinary. 2. Stay within a fair and accurate report of what has happened within court proceedings 3. Turn it around and focus on the case studies. Eric – do we have the ltter that summonses him to the investigating committee? JOY: no only their report where they say come and explain the 10 things we list as charges. EXCLUDED FROM STORY: After the court found against Bobroff he wrote a letter to the law society colleagues – Joy hasn’t included the comments from it in this cut BOBROFF INTERVIEW: Ronald says this is a vendetta by discovery and everyone is doing their bidding. If we get an interview with Bobroff, he will mention Discovery. We have Jonathan Broomberg at 5 tomorrow afternoon in case Ronald gives us an interview... Bobroff viewing 2 Wednesday 11 March 2015 9.30am GM, Eric, Joy, Tony, AC, WG 1. Duration should be 18 minutes 2. Bobroff chasing ambulance image should be removed. Rather use older footage of him. 3. Newsletter explanation is a bit confusing. Dumb this down. Bring out the points in bold in graphics where it actually states that on the newsletter. 4. R6 a copy is that industry standard? Check this. 5. Contingency agreement – see where it says 30% on document. Explain that act allows for 25% or double whichever is lower. 6. Take out Devi comment... “Let’s move on” in Bobroff interview. 7. Write around the issue that Bobroff charged for additional 16 hours after the case was settled on De Pontes. Add response from Bobroff here. 8. Law Society Certificate: bring it out and show the viewer what it says. Pull out words: partners never found guilty... 9. Take out other two people on Darren Bobroff picture 10. Where you say Anthony was unaware that he was signing 30% contract, explain the legal issues here about percentage. 11. Rather say “Bobroff ignored subsequent 2004 supreme court of appeal judgement which held...”. Use appeal court visuals here. 12. Quote Fabricius comment on de la Guerre matter. Include his name. 13. Take out double reference to “Plus Vat” on letter 14. Cover Anthony Millar’s numberplate 15. Add Devi asking Bobroff about charging for 16 hours after settlement was reached 16. 2 epilepsy comments on De La Guerre 17. Check on de la Guerre figure. R1.1-million or R969 000? Double check this. 18. Rather use law “reinterpreted” instead of re-engineered. 19. Don’t use image of Tony with De la Guerres 20. RAF victims could go back for recourse with interest going back all the 2002. Make this clearer. “Any claimant of the fund can go back....” 21. Discovery saying: no two sides. Take out. 22. RAF exterior shot rather than interior first 23. Leave out Paul O’ Sullivan 24. Let Cora explain more about being a Russian spy. Clarify her qualifications and she was in SA Navy. 25. confusing where you bring Jeanne in where you refer to Cora again as being moved into the accounts dept at the same time Jeanne’s case went to the Con Court. Legal: Eric van den Bergh 1. “If he is honest...” Can’t have like that. Take that commentary out. 2. Legally it is sound. 3. All comments are backed up. 4. Add: Even the constitutional court observed there was confusion in the legal profession about contingency fees. 5. Add he says everyone is doing it. He gave contingency agreements from others but none are signed. Put in a line that others are doing it too. We need to say he accuses others. 6. Take out Paul O’ Sullivan entirely and just say Bobroff accused her of theft. 7. Ask Bobroff for recording of Russian spy allegation. 8. Explain Cora was at an American University in Russia and that she was in SA Navy 9. Eric comfortable with link that says overreaching comes down to just plain stealing. Carte Blanche HD Nikola Vrahimis 25 March 2015 Press Release: No Press Release Script: FINAL TX SCRIPT BOBROFF 18th March 2015 Commentary One Spring 2007- On the P91 near Modderfontein. A driver, racing another smashes into the back of a Hu/nday Accent- two young men are in the back seat, one is killed instantly. The other, Anthony De Pontes barely survives. UP sound screech brakes Anthony I had broken my neck they wanted to amputate my arm and my chances of living weren’t too good Commentary Two This apprentice mechanic was paralysed on impact, leaving him confined to his parent’s home for the last eight years. Anthony You have to rely on people It’s everything hey. Dressing me, bathing me feeding me Commentary Three Anthony’s family came here to Ronald Bobroff and Partners to help them claim money from the Road Accident Fund. Link They trusted he would represent his son’s best interests Devi to RB So would you say you run a respectable and ethical business? Ronald Bobroff I believe so! I have been elected to the council of the law society and served as a president and held numerous offices within the profession Commentary Four But Ronald Bobroff’s image has been tarnished. For years he has been taking a flat percentage off the top of clients money recovered from the RAF. He has charged them common law contingency fees, but these fees are illegal. The De Pontes family didn’t know that. Attorney Anthony Millar explains Anthony Millar There is a 1000 years of law that says that type of agreement is prohibited and the reason for that is very simple- that when lawyers become shareholders in their clients cases the professional responsibility to their client and the courts becomes blurred because they now have a vested interest in the outcome of the case. Commentary Five In 2010 the RAF paid Anthony R6.1 million. Bobroff took R2.1 Million in fees, including vat. A court later found that Bobroff took R1.7 million more than he should have. Anthony also had to wait for the funds. Anthony De Pontes We nearly lost our house – because my parents had to pay for everything. It really put us in turmoil. Commentary Six But Bobroff rejects any allegations of impropriety and he has a Law Society certificate from 2013 as proof. Ronald Bobroff We have never had a finding against us of unprofessional conduct. EVER! Devi Link The legal profession has a delicate way of describing the theft of a client’s money, by one of their own – they call it over reaching, but when it comes down to it – its just plain stealing Commentary Seven Bobroff has been accused of over reaching by two whistleblowers who worked for him, attorney Anthony Millar, Legal journalist Tony Beamish and in January, an investigating committee of the law society. Devi The Law Society talks about prima facie evidence of over reaching which is what you say you don’t do? Ronald Unfortunately the Chair Mr Mayet seems to lack any understanding of the ruling by the law society on whose committee he actually sits! Commentary Eight The Contingency fee act said that attorneys could charge a maximum of 25% or double their normal fees whichever was the lower. Then in 2002 the law society allowed its attorneys to charge more, as long as they were reasonable. Bobroff says he was not alone in charging more. Bobroff As you know the law society issued a ruling in 2002 – /where it said its members are permitted and encouraged to charge straight contingency fees Devi But that is against the law Bobroff Well it wasn’t then Commentary nine But as far back as 2004, long before Antony even contacted Bobroff, a high court made a ruling. “Any contingency fee agreement, outside of the act is illegal.” Devi It sounds to me like the law said one thing, it was quite clear and lawyers like yourself and others took the gap? Ronald I disagree with that, there was not from then till late 2011 a single court decision saying that you could not have a valid common law contingency fee agreement Commentary Ten The De Pontes family eventually approached Anthony Millar. Anthony Millar Bobroff has taken everything from these clients except responsibility Commentary eleven He uncovered additional charges by Bobroff’s firm, which tricked Anthony into making a difficult and unnecessary journey to court, just so they could charge him for the time. Anthony Millar There were 16.5 hours of charges for days after the settlement had taken place Commentary twelve This is currently one of the counts Bobroff and Partners must answer to, at a discipline/ary enquiry of the Law Society. Devi to De Pontes Even if you are a really bad person it would be very difficult to do this to somebody? Anthony De Pontes Ya, only a monster would do something like this Commentary Thirteen Confirmation that Bobroff and partners were charging unlawfully high fees, would come unexpectedly via this beautiful young woman, flung through the back of a windscreen here, in 2005. Juanne I tried to open my eyes but I couldn’t see anything. Nothing! and then I heard my sister scream from far away: “Jeanne is dead, Jeanne is dead!” Commentary fourteen Jeannay De la Guerre survived but she’s a broken woman. A brain injury has left her with blackouts, sleeplessness, and on permanent anti-epileptic medication. Juanne You just feel like, you know the life is sucked out of you Commentary fifteen Juanne also signed Bobroff’s unlawful agreement. Of her R2.5 million payout from the RAF, Bobroff took over a million rand, gave her no bill to explain his costs and made her wait two years for part of her payout. Did you ever get that bill? Juanne No. Commentary Sixteen Juanne went to Anthony Millar and together they decided to challenge Bobroff’s agreement in court. Devi Where you not scared to take him on he is such a big lawyer? No. Why? Juanne Because I believe in the law Commentary Seventeen But the law was being reinterpreted here, at Bobroff’s office. Director Darren Bobroff’s letter appears to reverse engineer fees charged to Jeanne, nearly two years after the RAF had paid her out. PLEASE URGENTLY PREPARE AN ATTORNEY CLIENT BILL SO AS TO ENSURE THAT YOU CAN JUSTIFY THE HOURS FOR A TOTAL FEE PLUS VAT OF R1.1 MILLION Commentary eighteen But Ronald blames the secretary. Ronald She off her own bat used a standard letter Devi You have this as a standard letter? Ronald No, no, no- and she took that letter and she changed the wording and she will give evidence under oath that she was not instructed to use that terminology. It looks bad Ronald! This is what I am saying Ronald It does look bad and she has been reprimanded and apologized Why did you keep her? Because she is an excellent secretary Devi She is not very good Ronald Well she is good in other ways Commentary nineteen When Anthony requested Jeanne’s bill they were stunned to find a referral fee of R385 thousand paid to Darren Bobroffs wife Lisa, whom she had never met. Ronald blames the bookkeeper. Ronald We had a number of bookkeepers who were sadly not up to scratch. What this book keeper did she omitted to debit the fee but next to the cheque she put REF – Referral – there was no referral. Devi You are blaming staff again now Ronald It was the bookkeeper YES IT WAS! Devi Do you have competent people working here now? Ronald Very competent Devi Why did it go to Darren’s wife though? Ronald It was drawings for Darren Bobroff as a director and it was supposed to be deposited in his wife’s account, they were going to buy a property. Perfectly legitimate! Commentary twenty In Feb 2013 Juanne De La Guerre won her case against Bobroff. Judge Fabricius said that Bobroff …”must have been aware that the overwhelming view of distinguished authorities …was that any agreement not complying with the Act would be invalid, and could amount to unprofessional conduct.” Bobroff appealed and lost. DEVI link But despite those judgements Ronald Bobroff pushed on hoping that the Constitutional Court would make a different ruling, but alas for Mr Bobroff they were unequivocal. Commentary Twenty one The court confirmed that flat % fees charged by Bobroff and others, had always been illegal. But they also acknowleged confusion around fees. Bobroff reads judgement Uncertainty reigned in the attorneys profession! Devi Irrespective you were wrong The CC has said so Ronald Twelve years after the decision was taken Devi Which decision your decision? Ronald The Law Society Devi The Law Society cannot supercede the law? Ronald It can’t. Devi Thank you! Commentary twenty-two The ruling means that any RAF victims charged these contingency fees outside the act can go back to their lawyers and reclaim the difference with interest. Devi You weren’t happy. Ronald No Devi In fact you called it disastrous Yes Devi For who? Ronald For attorneys who acted in good faith in accordance with Law Society guidelines Commentary twenty- three The law Society declined an interview with Carte Blanche. They supported Bobroff in his case against Juanne De La Guerre. Devi Did the Law society protect Ronald Bobroff Anthony Millar I believe so yes … Devi How do you feel about that you belong to that same society? Anthony Millar I am embarrassed! I am embarrassed at the position! Commentary twenty- four Last year legal journalist Tony Beamish pounded out over thirty articles on Bobroff for Moneyweb. Tony now works at Carte Blanche and Bobroff believes we have employed a stooge of Discovery Health. Ronald He is singling me out because Discovery has this vendetta against me and me alone. Commentary Twenty- five For anything other than illness he says Discovery Health will try to wriggle out of paying your claim. Ronald If you require any med care, your neighbors dog bites you, the police assault you, you fall in a hole you are not entitled to any benefits whatsoever and Discovery do enforce that. Its immoral, its illegal, its wrong and by me exposing them Discovery have declared war on me Commentary Twenty-six But CEO Jonathan Broomberg says Bobroff’s story is dishonest. To prove his point he says Discovery Health has paid out 30 000 road accident victims since 2006. Jonathan Out of 30 000 we have paid …out find me one who has anything to say apart from this one man and one practice, of the 1100 RAF attorneys find me one who is complaining …you will not find one Devi So what is the deal here? Jonathan What I think is happening is he is throwing dust in the air, accusing every tom dick and harry of having a vendetta against him – you ask yourself why he is doing that – I would say its to distract attention from his behavior and his practice behavior. Commentary Twenty-seven But that is not how Cora Van Der Merwe saw it. A loyal cost consultant employed at Bobroff and partners, Cora felt a duty to protect her boss against Discovery Health and Tony Beamish. Cora At one stage he said there is this big vendetta and he will even start crying to get sympathy and your whole heart will go out to him Commentary Twenty-eight Later Cora was moved into the legal cost department, and suddenly had access to the legers and the control files. Things just didn’t add up. Cora Then I realized that there were a lot of things that concerned me and I got frightened you know. Devi Link Apart from the over reaching Cora claims she found evidence of vat fraud, and falsified documents Commentary Twenty-nine She also alleges the fees from RAF payments run into millions. Cora Well I have evidence that their fees alone in the past 12 months were R49 million. …She smiles… they are 42 years in business Commentary Thirty Last year the RAF paid R4.7 billion just in legal fees, but how much have they paid to Ronald Bobroff and partners? Eugene Watson, CEO signed an affidavit in 2013, listing the money they paid to Bobroff and partners over ten years. Eugene Watson CEO RAF I think in terms of our figures we showed that almost a billion rand was paid in compensation for over 3000 claims and more than 25% was deemed to be a contingency claim. Ronald If it was a billion rand, and I don’t know if it was it represents the damages to our clients, the cost payable to our experts, to our advocates and the amount of our fees. It would certainly not be 25% of a billion rand!! Devi Would it be more? Ronald No nonsense! Nowhere near that!! Commentary Thirty- one Anthony Millar has eight cases against Bobroff. He has broken ranks with the Law Society to tackle Bobroff head on, believing this may be the biggest legal fraud in SA history. Anthony I believe we are looking at a R270 million rand fraud at this stage just with what we know Commentary Thirty- two By mid 2014 Cora decided to blow the whistle on Bobroff. She felt the Law Society was compromised, and instead made a protected disclosure to journalist Tony Beamish, who she now trusted. Devi You accused her of theft Ronald She did steal yes. She downloaded electronic information and its probably industrial espionage, but criminal charges will be laid Commentary Thirty-three He goes further. Cora could be a Russian agent says Bobroff. Ronald I have recordings where she comes to me and says Mr B I want to open my heart to you I have been communicating with Mr Beamish I was trained in counter espionage in the SA navy and I was sent to Russia to train Devi She said that to you Ronald I have a recording I will make it available to you and she says I have been corresponding with him and I have gained his confidence Devi She is a secret agent? Ronald That is what she says Commentary thirty- four Bobroff never did give Carte Blanche those recordings. While Cora denies being an agent, she admits to studying in Russia in the early 90’s. Devi Have you ever been a Russian spy? No Have you been to Russia? Yes Commentary Thirty- five By end of Feb last year three levels of the SA judiciary had found Bobroff’s practice illegal, yet Yasmin Motara was still billed using the illegal agreement. Devi So what did Ronald Do? Did Ronald stop doing this? Ronald Indeed we did. Commentary Thirty six When a driver skipped a red light on Snake road, he smashed into Yasmin - her car struck a pole and split in half. Extensive brain injuries forced her to give up her career in politics. Now she just makes it through the day as a teacher. YASMIN I have to figure out who is this new me- what cant she do today- what can she get right today, and I try to hide it, because I don’t want people to pity me- but don’t think for a moment that it is not all kinds of hard. Commentary thirty seven Yasmin received R6.5 million rand from the RAF, minus Bobroff’s fees of R1.8 million Yasmin Well they said don’t worry its R1.8 but we will furnish you with the bill- I haven’t received anything yet – I never heard from Bobroff. Pffff! Commentary Thirty eight But Cora had worked on her bill and knew that Yasmin should have paid no more than R362 000, not the R1.8 million that Bobroff had charged her. In December, Cora took Yasmin through the actual charges. YASMIN It was so blatant! It was so much! Like photocopies –over R50 000! Really, I would have photocopied it myself. Commentary thirty nine Yasmin is currently in a battle with Bobroff to recover some of the funds. Yasmin And no one is going to make a buck off my injury! …while RBP get rich!! Devi But Anthony it’s the same story over and again? Anthony Yes Devi its groundhog day! It’s the same case over and over with the same attorney crying conspiracy and vendetta and all sorts of things, none of it dealing with the bottom line fact that these RAF victims have been grossly over charged on a basis that is illegal Devi Don’t you feel bad Ronald Not at all I feel proud of what we have done That you took money from people and you were wrong about it and we know you were wrong Ronald They got a very good legal service at no cost to themselves in accordance with what the law was understood to be at the time Devi And this would have continued if it was not for the De la Guerre matter Ronald Everyone would have continued Devi And that is not right! Ronald I disagree I think it was a great service to the public and I am confident govt will amend the CFA act to make provision for a straight %. Commentary forty In the meantime Bobroff is digging deep into his pockets. He has just repaid Anthony De Pontes R3 million including R700 000 in interest by order of a court, and at least another half a million rand to Jeanne De La Guerre. But what of his other cases going back to 2002? Devi And are you not going to go back and find those cases Ronald Definitely not Devi And you don’t feel you should from a moral point of view Ronald I can’t begin to understand why you would say that? Devi I can’t begin to understand why you insist that you wont! Ronald Well that is where we differ THE END Invoicing Back references from Insert ID in Invoice: Title Author Last Updated Invoice for Bobroff fall from grace (4492) Joy Summers 19 March 2015
